summary: Missing hourly buffer credit after hosted fallback during reserved capacity saturation
estimated_impact: Customer was underbilled by uncredited hourly buffer; produced a provisional invoice shortfall and alerted finance. Affects one dedicated org during two fallback windows.
description:
Issue summary:
BrightLens contacted Support reporting that their March 1-7 provisional invoice shows no hourly buffer credit for two windows where their Dedicated pool saturated and requests fell back to hosted. Impact:
- Missing hourly buffer credit on provisional invoice causing apparent overage for customer
- Customer concerned invoice will finalize without expected credit applied
Environment:
- Dedicated pool org-id: org-brightlens-01 (dedicated)
- Region: us-east-1
- Timeframe: 2026-03-02 01:40 - 2026-03-02 02:15 UTC and 2026-03-05 22:05 - 2026-03-05 22:55 UTC
Steps to reproduce / Observed behavior:
1) Dedicated pool saturated -> smart routing sent traffic to hosted fallback variant
2) Serving runtime returned hosted responses; postbacks were emitted with fallback_tag:hosted and original_queue:dedicated
3) Billing postback reconciler processed hosted usage but did not apply the org-level hourly buffer credit for those fallback intervals
Expected behavior:
- When dedicated traffic falls back to hosted, hourly buffer credits tied to the consumer org should still be consumed/applied for the fallback usage (per pricing policy)
Actual behaviour:
- Hosted usage lines present, but hourly buffer credit lines missing for those intervals. Finance shows a provisional overage for BrightLens.
Attached logs and artifacts:
- sample postback JSONs (postbacks_redacted_20260302.ndjson)
comments: 2026-03-10 10:12 - Support (Priya): Customer reports missing hourly buffer credits after fallback. Attached provisional invoice and sample postbacks. Requested urgent investigation and provisional credit hold.

2026-03-10 11:05 - Billing (Marta): Confirmed hosted usage lines exist in provisional invoice. I don't see a buffer credit line for those timestamps; opening reconciler trace. Linking to reconciler PRs and runbook.

2026-03-10 14:22 - SRE (Ethan): Found postback entries with fallback_tag=hosted and original_queue=dedicated. Reconciler filters hourly_buffer eligibility by queue tag; looks like filter excludes fallback records. Hypothesis: filter uses queue==dedicated strictly instead of original_queue field.
2026-03-11 09:30 - Support (Priya): Customer acknowledged and asked whether a provisional waiver can be issued while we fix the reconciler. Also asked for a short-term manual adjustment timeline.
2026-03-12 16:10 - Billing (Marta): Willing to apply provisional credit for affected period once SRE provides list of postback ids. Finance needs estimate of delta before manual credit.

2026-03-12 17:30 - SRE (Ethan): Provided CSV of 1,124 affected postback ids and estimated buffer credit = $1,872. Next step: deploy reconciler patch to include original_queue and rerun postback ingestion for affected window.
investigation_notes: Initial triage: confirmed hosted usage lines present in provisional invoice; no matching buffer credit entries for the two outage windows.
Hypothesis: billing reconciler eligibility check uses queued_queue attribute, not original_queue, therefore fallback events tagged as hosted lost the dedicated-buffer attribution.

Ran local reconcile replay on a snapshot: when feeding postbacks with original_queue=dedicated the buffer credit algorithm emitted expected credit line. When original_queue absent or ignored, no credit was emitted.

Found code path in invoice-reconciler where fallback_tag logic not populating billing_queue in normalized record. Edge-case when request routed by Smart Router -> hosted variant done at gateway layer and gateway prepends fallback_tag but does not set billing_queue field.

Root cause: mismatch between Smart Router fallback metadata and reconciler normalization contract. Reconciler expects billing_queue field; gateway sets original_queue but an earlier normalization step dropped it for hosted postbacks.
Risk assessment: low risk to runtime; only affects postback processing path. Fix impacts reconciler ingestion and replay pipeline.
resolution:
Workaround and fix plan:
1) Short-term: Billing will apply provisional manual credit of $1,872 to BrightLens while fix is deployed (Finance note FIN-2026-03-BL-01).
2) Fix: deploy reconciler patch to propagate original_queue into normalized billing_queue for fallback-tagged postbacks. PR #873 created and reviewed.
3) Re-run ingestion for affected windows and regenerate provisional invoice lines; postback replay job scheduled for 2026-03-13 02:00 UTC.
4) Post-deploy validation run against sample postbacks and customer confirmation.
Follow-ups:
- Add unit tests covering fallback metadata paths.
- Update Smart Router -> Reconciler contract doc in Confluence.
- Monitor next billing run for similar anomalies and create alert on mismatch between fallback_tag counts and buffer credit lines.
